items.title: CoStar’s Stock Popped. Can Earnings Keep the Momentum Going?
items.summary: CoStar Group  stock on Monday jumped ahead of earnings.  CoStar  stock closed at $29.17 on Monday, up 5.5%, the largest gain since July 16, according to Dow Jones Market Data.  CoStar is “the ‘Bloomberg of commercial real estate (CRE) data,’” BMO Capital Markets analysts Jeffrey Silber and Ryan Griffin wrote in a July 17 note, referring to the Bloomberg financial data terminal widely used by Wall Street.

items.title: Software Is Beating Chips for Once. It May Not Be a Flash in the Pan.
items.summary: Enterprise software providers, many left behind in the artificial-intelligence boom, were the apparent beneficiaries of a pullback in chip and hardware stocks.  Workday  the human-resources software provider, was the top performer in the large-cap index on Monday, jumping 9.3%.  Altogether, the much-watched  exchange-traded fund, or IGV, rose 4%, while the  ETF, or SOXX, slumped 3.1%.

items.title: How CoStar’s CFO Transition And Cost Focus At CoStar Group (CSGP) Has Changed Its Investment Story
items.summary: Earlier this month, CoStar Group announced that long‑time executive Robin Rossmann will become Chief Financial Officer on July 31, 2026, replacing Christian Lown, who is leaving to pursue an opportunity outside the real estate information industry. Rossmann’s track record of cutting about US$51,000,000 in European costs while expanding revenue and launching CoStar in France highlights the finance chief’s deep operational experience and international focus.
